chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Roy Eldridge, Mary Lou Williams, Litton Garner and Babe Russin
summary: Pittsburgh musicians she knew or didn't, and Babe Russin's presence on her first record.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: How about other musicians like Roy Eldridge who you mentioned before?
Yeah, well Roy had left Pittsburgh before I got popular. But I knew Roy and everything.
Mary Lou, I know of Mary Lou.
No, only after I got to New York. But I knew Mary Lou was from Pittsburgh. I worked, I get a couple of those little digs with an older brother of Erroll Garner.

No, another one that never became popular. He stayed around Pittsburgh. And then there was a very popular drummer around Pittsburgh by the name of 'Honey Boy'. And a piano player I know, Nini Waters. Of course now, I remember by this time I was becoming familiar with some of the local musicians and I think Billy Eckstine was working with one of the local big bands in Pittsburgh before he got his own band, and before he went with Earl Hines. But I don't remember

There is one name I'd like to ask you about, he turned up on your first recording session, and that's Babe Russin.
Yeah. You know I didn't know it was Babe Russin from Pittsburgh.
Well that's the information I have from the Encyclopedia of Jazz.

Well, I think that how Babe Russin got in on the gig, Claude must have known him because I knew none of the musicians before I came to New York. You know, I didn't even know Kirby that well and his group. In fact, the first record date that I had used John Kirby's men, he had along with Babe, Pete Brown, alto Man, and Frankie Newton. He hadn't got a hold of Charlie Shavers and Russell Procope at that time. In fact, I think that Billy Kyle, Russell Procope, and Charlie with out on the road with Lucky Millinder and his band at the time. So when they came back Charlie grabbed them. And I just took it for granted that Babe Russin was one of Claude's friends.
